summary: A short pilot on Adolf Hitler's personal oddities: his obsessive teenage crush in Austria, his 1920s trench coat and dog whip, his chronic flatulence, and the untested drugs his doctor Theodor Morell fed him through World War II.

evidence.note: Host frames the episode around Hitler as an odd young man in his twenties and thirties, not a life story
Kubizek, Hitler's teenage friend, and his memoir introduced as the source for the youth segment
1905 walk where Hitler first sees the girl he fixates on for about four years; earliest dated period
1920s Munich: trench coat, trilby and the whip he carried for a decade
1936: Morell takes Hitler on as a patient to treat his flatulence
Morell gives Hitler dozens of untested drugs, many made by his own firms
Rotation of morphine, methamphetamine and cocaine injections through 1943-1945

notes: partial_life set: a 16-minute pilot framed by title, description and host around young Hitler's oddities and his flatulence, not a biography; birth, childhood and the war itself get no airtime. Covered span runs from the 1905 Kubizek anecdote to the 1945 drug regime. Main span 1920-1945 (whip era to death) is approximate. Kubizek's segment is about 2.5 minutes, kept as secondary.
